1.t: The interrelated musical families: Barbarins, Arthidores, Tapos, Fraziers
1.s: He counts forty-some musicians in the extended family, discusses Louis Arthidore, Big Belly Fob, Lionel Tapo, the Bigeou spasm band and other New Orleans musical families.
1.ch: Second session: family, Armstrong and David Jones
1.q: And I had a uncle. Great clarinet player. He was a virtuoso. Louis Arthidore. That’s my grandmother’s maiden name. Her younger brother.

1.s: Lu's father August DuPont, called Dimes, played sax, and relatives included a drummer cousin and clarinetist Gil Thomas.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: August Du Pont is his name. They called him Dimes. All the musicians would call him Dimes. He played. And my cousin Hersey(?), he played drums. And he has a son, they call him Bib, but his right name is [INDECIPHERABLE]

1.t: Cousins on Danny's genealogy list: Clemons, Taphole, Arthadeaux, Perez
1.s: Danny explains the list of relatives who played music: Octavia Clemons, Lydell Taphole, Charlie Lajoie, Howard Randolph, Arthur Arthadeaux, and Manuel Perez.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: No, there are no more Arthadeaux. Louis was the youngest brother. And there was Arthur Arthadeaux. We used to call him Artur; Artur(?) in patois. A really fine looking man. They had sisters, and they've got some of them out in the country.

1.t: Louis Arthadeaux, the clarinet virtuoso great-uncle
1.s: Danny tells of his grandmother's brother, a clarinet virtuoso who wrote waltzes and died of a social disease around 1905.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: Well, it should have had about six more. There's Lucien Barbarin, Junior; Charlie Barbarin, Junior, and their little nephew, what's his name...

1.t: Louis Barbarin's daughter, Louis Nelson and the Biblical genealogy
1.s: They joke that the family tree reads like Matthew, with Barbarin, Santiago, Marrero, Williams and Frazier families all intertwined.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: Louis Nelson is a trombone player here, and he had a brother who played saxophone. I don't know his brother's name. I can't think of it now. I knew it years ago.

1.t: Brother Cornbread and the Bijou cousins
1.s: Danny describes cousin Joseph Thomas, clarinetist, and the vaudeville star Esther Bijou and her brother Boy Bijou, related to the Barbarins.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: Esther Bijou and Boy Bijou. That's her brother. Boy Bijou playd kazoo and the clarinet. He was a ballroom musician, played the ballroom with a band called the Rootie-Dooty sometimes.

139.s: He talks about his only brother, a riverfront worker, and a stepbrother who is a mechanic.
139.q: I got one brother can't whistle. Don't know how to whistle. Never, don't know no nothing but a river front. Why he works? He works out of the river front. Get out of the river front. Don't know no other ways but a river front. Been out there 26 years.

139.t: His sons and the lack of other musicians in the family
139.s: His son plays piano and has a band in New York, and Sing is the only musician in the family.
139.q: My son played more piano than me but he don't play what I play.

139.s: Talk of a left-handed stepbrother and Narvin Kimball's left-handed banjo playing at Preservation Hall.
139.q: Well, he had a thing that go on one time. But I don't know, he got the devil in him, you know, try to buy a house. That got away from him. He tried to play piano but I told him, you know, I said I never seen a left hand piano play yet, man. I've never seen a left hand piano play, man. I've seen a…

198.t: Musical relatives on his mother's side
198.s: His father played no instrument, but cousins on his mother's side did, including the Marrero family and the Frazier brothers, a piano player and drummers.
198.q: No, he didn't play any instrument at all. My daddy didn't. But part of my family played on my mother's side. All of them, John, Moreland, Eddie. They were all related to you, weren't they? Yeah. That's all cousins. All cousins? Yeah, that's on my mother's side. Then on my mother's side again, I got…

198.t: Uncle Tartone and the Marrero and Frazier cousins
198.s: Barnes lists musical relatives: his uncle, the Marrero cousins, the Fraziers, Dave Williams and an aunt who played guitar.
198.ch: Blind Charlie, kin and early memories
198.q: What did he play? Something. Was he Sugar? He played with Black Patty. Sure, you know. What was his last name? No, I'll tell you.

198.s: Barnes describes Ninny, who left town long ago, and compares his playing and build with Pills's.
198.q: Yeah, Ninny Quacko. Well, Ninny Quacko was, uh, was alright, but, uh, he didn't bother much with us. You see? It was a guy mistaken. The Ninny went off, and Ninny Quacko went off here with a shoe. Mm-hmm. That's years ago. And, uh, you know, we never heard, uh, once, I believe we heard from him…

653.s: His brothers and sisters picked up instruments and put them down; a granddaughter may take up clarinet.
653.q: Now some of them like to sing, you know. Right. I don't know where they can sing but I hope they just keep to their nursing and hairdressing jobs. It will be much better. But nobody at my deceased I imagine, they won't have any musicians following. Maybe my granddaughter has decided that she would…

653.t: The many Baptiste musician families of New Orleans
653.s: He knows about 35 Baptistes who all play music, including Earl, Alvin, Harold and Lionel, and doubts they are all related.
653.q: There's Earl Baptiste. Quentin. Earl Quentin Baptiste who's gone. There's Alvin Baptiste. There's Harold Baptiste. There's Lionel Baptiste. There's the whole Baptiste brothers family.

865.t: In-laws: Richard McLean and the Barbarins; loud drums and active playing
865.s: No other relatives played music except in-laws such as Richard McLean, who played with Kid Rena. He says he likes to stay active behind the drums.
865.ch: Music as a way of life
865.q: I got all my in-laws, a lot of them. Richard McLean, he married my niece, Beatrice, who died there. She died about a couple of months ago. Oh yes, I remember that.

865.t: Family name spelling and relatives; brother-in-law Bob Riley
865.s: Phillips says his father played trumpet, confirms spelling, denies kinship with other Phillips musicians, and mentions his brother-in-law.
865.q: No, Joe Phillips, no, not the kid in the end. No, no, no, no. Bob Riley's his brother-in-law. My brother-in-law is Bob Riley. Poor yes. Louis Bob Riley, the one that stayed across the street here. Poor yes. Paul Bob Riley.

192.t: Brothers, cousins and aunts and uncles in the Fraser family
192.s: He names his other brothers, piano-playing cousins and his father's siblings.
192.q: Yeah, well, I have another brother which died in 49. My name is Alec Fraser. He was a piano player. He started off... Dave Williams, the piano player now playing in the French quarters. And he started a cousin of mine who died, too, called Mitchell Fraser. That was my father's youngest brother,…

192.t: Fraser family ties to the Barnes and Morrell musicians
192.s: He explains that the Barnes and Morrell musicians' mothers were his father's Fraser sisters.
192.q: Related. Well, Milly Barnes and Paul Barnes, their mother was my father's sister. And John Morrell, Simon Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, Eddie Morrell, all musicians. Their mother was my father's sister from the Fraser.

896.t: The Darensbourg family and Willie Foster
896.s: Russell asks about Joe Darensbourg and Willie Foster; Roubleau says Caffrey's family came from his hometown, his father played mandolin and guitar, and Caffrey died in Texas.
896.q: Willie Foster. Willie Foster. His first instrument that I could recall, or I would, was a violin. That's right. He said he played violin. From a violin, then he started playing guitar in the banjo with a foster.

896.t: Surviving members of his father's band and uncles
896.s: None of the old hometown band is alive; only one of nine uncles survives and only his father played music.
896.q: Not a soul living. Not a one of them. Not one. Not a soul living. About a soul living stuff. About a soul living stuff. brothers they only have one living and he didn't play any music yeah one of your uncles

868.s: De De recalls working with Burnell Santiago and his brother Lester 'Black', a musical family of which only those two played jobs.
868.q: Well, I did work a lot with Kid. You know, with I know this, uh, Brennel. Brennel Sonniac? Oh, yeah. He worked with the past few years. That's how we used to put him on the stool.

175.t: His saxophonist brother and his mother's address
175.s: His older brother played alto sax; he gives his mother's Dumaine Street address so the interviewer can contact him.
175.q: Well offhand I don't know his address, I'll have to look for it. Of course I could give you my mother's house and you could always contact him from there.

864.t: Tillman's musician cousins and in-laws, Batiste, Casmes, Gaudet
864.s: Allen follows up on Bill Russell's earlier interview: Joe Batiste, the Casme brothers and Hunter Allen Gaudet, Tillman's sister's husband; Vernon Gilbert is not kin.
864.q: Well, Joe Batiste played and John played and John got Sam Casme played and William Casme played. Those were John's brothers? All my first cousins, yeah. Yeah.

622.t: Earlier Chicago generation: Quartell, Don Murray and Glenn Scoville
622.s: They discuss Quartell's brothers, tenor players Murray and Scoville, and how Murray began.
622.q: Tinny Scoville, Glenn Scoville, was another tenor player who was a contemporary of Don Murray's. Don Murray used to play a scene melody in a Presbyterian church in Evanston. That's how he got started. And then he changed to clarinet when he joined Go Cat. But he and Scoville both played with the…

880.t: Brothers Henry, Willie 'Kaiser' and Nelson Joseph
880.s: Joseph names his younger brother Henry, who played with Freddie Landry, and his brothers Willie (called Kaiser) and Nelson.
880.q: No, I have a younger brother who played music too in the country. Henry Josephs used to play with Phil Bonne William. Oh, yes. He played with Freddie Landry. I played with Freddie Landry. Freddie Landry played with Freddie Landry. After he got his own band.

253.t: Brothers Robert, Edward, Clarence and Herbert
253.s: Hall describes his brothers' instruments and jobs, his singing sister, and a trumpet-playing uncle.
253.q: Yeah, well I have Mount Woolley's brother, Robert, he was, he was one of them, he was a really good musician. He used to play tenor, played clarinet, I think he played a little piano.

474.t: Non-musical family and kinsman Richard M. Jones
474.s: No other musicians in his family except Richard M. Jones, a pianist related on his father's side.
474.ch: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
474.q: more musicians? None musical. What was your mother's name? Earlene Jones. Earlene Jones. The only other musician I had, the richer you know I had in my family was Richard M. Jones. Yeah. And what did he play when you knew him? Richard M. Jones played the piano and they told me that he played the…

34.s: Burns names brother Tom (James) Boynes, a piano player in New Orleans, and dead brother Robert.
34.q: Yeah. You got a brother too? Is he still living? Yeah, he's living. He's in New Orleans. Oh, in New Orleans. What's his name? He played piano, funky butts. We call him the funky butts. What's his name? James Boynes. We call him Tom. Oh, yeah. Everybody know him in Tomy Boynes.

724.s: Lists nephews on bass, drums, banjo and trombone, one playing rock and roll.
724.q: Yeah. I think he played a job or two here on the bass. And if he went to California, he took up a band shift, a ghetto, a ghetto and a bass. And I was told that he was playing older than good. How long did you stay on Harbridge Street? I don't remember. I must have stayed there about five or six…

827.t: Half brothers John, Cooney, Man and Boy in the district
827.s: Arthur describes his father's other family: half brothers, three pianists and a drummer, who worked in the red light district.
827.q: He was a half brother of mine, on my father's side. Now there was John, there was another brother by the name of Cooney, and there was another brother by the name of Boy.

848.t: Andrew Kimball and the Kimball brothers
848.s: Discovering that trumpeter Andrew Kimball was his father's brother, and the singing quartet of brothers.
848.ch: Henry Kimball and the Kimball family
848.q: So, I should have known. I didn't know that they were related until after I had started to play music. And I met Andrew Kimball and Mrs. Margaret Kimball in Shreveport. And Bill Matthews, the trombone player, came to me and told me that he wanted to, that Mr. Kimball wanted to talk with me. And I…

863.t: His large family and the bandleader 'Two Roads'
863.s: He had ten siblings, mostly living nearby; asked about a bandleader of a similar name, he says he knows no such person and claims he put every musician before the public.
863.q: It's a great family. I got six living now and one Eve. Six sisters living and one Eve.

1051.t: Baquet's relatives, his sister's chicken coop and pictures
1051.s: Talk of other relatives and musicians, Baquet's sister's place on Bienville, and the lack of pictures of a cousin.
1051.q: Dad is standing up here in my house. He said, but I can't be all your spots. Yeah. I mean, he'd stay over the lake.

921.s: Her father had no musical brothers; his father Eusebio played guitar for amusement; none of her brothers or sons play.
921.q: No. Uh, yes, I think he did. He played the guitar. But I think more so for himself. Just, uh, you know, to amuse himself. He didn't go out and make a living at it like my father did.

259.s: Allen asks who Chiff's brother was; Vincent names Thornwell and says Chiff's kid played guitar, bass, violin and cornet.
259.q: Who was Chiff's brother? Who? Chiff's brother. Chiff's brother? Chiff, Chiff. Who was Chiff's brother? He was Thornwell. What did he play? Thornwell, Matthew, and Thornwell. What did he play? Just a thorn there. Could he play any other instrument? Could he play any other instrument? No, that's…

627.t: Uncle Simon Carney and sister Rosalie Gibson
627.s: Williams says his uncle Simon Carney played with a knife and sang about a gambling man, and gives the address of his guitar-playing sister in New Orleans.
627.ch: Williams on guitarists, family and touring
627.q: Did he play with you? Simon Carney, yes, he was a guitar player. But the most that he played was with a knife, you see? About to sing about the gambling man, the biggest I ever heard him play, gambling man.

83.t: More Matassa relatives in the directories
83.s: They identify his father, Vincent's children and an uncle by marriage in Mississippi.
83.q: Yeah, there was another daughter. And there was a John... John Jay was also a son of Vincent Matassa. My father was John C. So John Jay on Charter Street would have been the son of Vincent Matassa. And John Matassa on Dauphine Street would have been my father.

41.t: Who else could be interviewed about Paul and Rappolo
41.s: Mares says his brother Rene and Rappolo's family could add little.
41.q: to the jazz. You were the nearest teenage to him. That's right. I stayed with it. No, my brother Rene is right back. He's right back. Oh, yeah. But he know any other more details of him? No, he wouldn't know because he didn't follow that. He didn't have the interest in the music. That's right. He…

873.t: Hall family: Edward, Clarence, Herbert, and uncle T-Man
873.s: Edward Hall is one of the brothers; Clarence and Herbert started on banjo, and their uncle T-Man played guitar in the band.
873.q: See when Clarence left, we took Herbert in his place. And he just picked it up and in a little while he could read faster than the uncles.

151.t: Nellie Lutcher's family band and drummer Elric Joseph
151.s: Reason names Lutcher's brothers and father in Lake Charles and tells of Elric Joseph, whom he later sent for in Indianapolis.
151.q: He was from, he was born in Louisiana, but most of his folks lived down in Galveston, Texas. Because when I sent for the band, for my little group down here to come to Indianapolis, Indiana, it was Elric Joseph that I had sent for. Mm-hmm. See, because I figured I couldn't get Freddie. Freddie was…

43.s: No other sisters sang. She knows of no musicians on her father's side, because she did not know that part of the family.
43.ch: Names, influences and early blues singers
43.q: Not that I know of. Not that I know of. Because there's a lot of my family on my father's side that I don't know. No, I don't know, so I don't know whether they, you know, was any singers among them.

45.t: Mac Lacey the drummer and the Devoiney family
45.s: They discuss drummer Mac Lacey, his brother Joe, and the musical Devoiney family.
45.ch: Piron, Pichon and the boat bands
45.q: Yeah, well I went to Fisk School right there, you know, and he stayed around the corner. I was just going to see him pretty regular.

664.t: The Miller family of musicians and Charlie Miller at the Frolic
664.s: They sort out which Millers are related, and Charlie Miller's trombone with Sharkey at the Frolic in the early twenties.
664.ch: Leaving music: Klessy and the Millers
664.q: Yeah...they got a...a group of Millers...they got Eddie... Eddie...uh...Eddie...the...the...the...the...tenor man...he's from here too... Uh-huh...and...is uh...is a...miller trombone player...

281.t: The Brunis brothers Henry and Merritt
281.s: They discuss George's brothers who were at the Friars Inn; Spanier vaguely recalls them and says George is plenty good.
281.q: I think I probably heard him once or twice, but it's very vague.

176.t: Which sisters played and with whom
176.s: Billie goes through Edna, Mabel, Della, Sadie and Ida, who played church, house parties or bands, plus Ida's musician son.
176.q: Edna's in, she's in Florida. She's out there, she's out about, she's around a casino, I don't know, a casino or somewhere out there on the Gulf. She's working out there, you know, in a hotel out there. But she's not playing the music out there, she's working out there now. They said where she was…

291.t: Musicians on both sides: Frazier, Marrero and Barnes cousins
291.s: He describes his father's guitar playing and the many musical cousins on his mother's side, the Fraziers and Marreros, and one cousin on his father's side.
291.q: My father was, he could play music also, it was on both sides. He used to play a guitar, but not in a band, you know. He played around the house and played guitar and singing. There was a musical there on both sides. And my mother's sister, she was very musical too, she played the guitar. Now…

884.t: Remus and Bill Matthews of Algiers
884.s: Remus Matthews, who played in church; where his widow lives; Bill Matthews who took up drums and played with a trumpeter called Lego and then Punch's string band.
884.q: Well, he used to live right here on Bellwood Street. You ever passed that funeral home right there? Oh, yeah. My funeral home? Hello? Funeral home right there, right in the back of the funeral home is Bellwood Street. Well, he used to live right there. His wife is right there now. Oh, yeah? Yeah,…

831.t: His brothers Arnold, Jack and Bud and their instruments
831.s: He names three musical brothers and what each played, including Jack the left-handed trombonist.
831.q: Well, Bud played mandolin. He played guitar. He played a little drum. He played a little bass. He played a little violin. Arnold played a little piano, bass, drum. Guitar, mandolin.

270.t: Richard M. Jones, Dave Perkins, his father's friends and cousin Peter Raphael
270.s: Asked about Donaldsonville-area musicians, he names Jones, Porter, Dave Perkins as a teacher of white and colored pupils, and his father's friends, then explains that Aunt Bella is the mother of drummer Peter Raphael, his first cousin.
270.q: Richard John. I heard him. Miney, they called him. Miney, yeah, yeah, yeah. Well, he's, I think he's the way or could avoid me, but I heard him talk about it. Now, there's another fellow that I remember, since we were speaking about that, uh, I met, he, uh, he, uh, he, uh, like the late John…

301.s: Dutre identifies his two musical uncles; Russell notes Baby Dodds called Honore 'Nora'.
301.q: Honoree. Because I know Baby Dodds in Chicago who worked with him always called him Nora.

833.t: Other musicians nearby, his family and the Robinson name
833.s: No family played music; he is unrelated to Jim or Ike Robinson.
833.ch: Mente's factory, hard times and later life
833.q: died as quite a kid i was in this year about 20 years old since he died any brothers that played any music no i had a brother but he didn't play he was a ball player he was yeah yeah he's a good one too

708.t: Other musicians named Christian, unrelated to her husband
708.s: Allen notes Charlie, Tommy and Buddy Christian in the discography; none are related. She remarks that many musicians came from New Orleans.
708.ch: St. Cyr, Dreamland and the OK festival
708.q: Uh-huh. Most of them... You know, so many musicians are from New Orleans.

133.t: David Williams's family names: Mary Lou, Noble Sissle and a bass-playing father
133.s: Walton and Brower talk about Williams's Trinidadian accent, his bassist father John Buddy and siblings named for Mary Lou Williams and Noble Sissle, with an aside about the Sissle and Blake book.
133.q: Oh yeah, they, they conversed. They're inseparable when you, when you, uh, when, when they come together. And uh, Dave's uh father was a bass player. And uh, his name was …

142.t: His brother and sister did not become musicians
142.s: His brother played piano and sax but became a painter-minded person; only he and his father were professional musicians.
142.q: He used to play the piano and then he learned to play the saxophone. He was never a musician in his heart; he never wanted to be a musician. And I don’t blame him. [Both laugh] No he developed some other things. He liked painting. that type of thing.

378.t: Mildred Bailey's brothers Chuck and Miles Rinker
378.s: Al Rinker is Mildred's brother; Norvo describes brother Chuck Rinker, a song plugger, and meeting Miles Rinker, a saxophonist, without knowing he was Mildred's brother.
378.ch: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
378.q: Well Chuck she brought in New York, didn't you meet him, he used to work, Mildred brought him in from California, he had a -- he had a trio with Bob Crosby and ah -- oh, what's his name, I can't remember his name now, he was married to Lorraine Day for awhile, he was a pilot, he's an Alaskan pibt…

29.t: The Brooks family: Dudley, Bert and the bathhouse
29.s: They sort out Dudley Brooks's brothers and recall that their father ran a bathhouse.
29.ch: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
29.q: Dudley, he took a little sick and wasnt very well, so Dudley quit playing, he quit playing.
